key_insight: ScaFE turns an LLM into a knowledge-driven feature engineer that converts scar images into clinically meaningful, interpretable features instead of using the model as a black-box classifier.
clinical_relevance: This could help distinguish keloids from hypertrophic scars with less labeled data while keeping raw images local and aligning outputs with established scar assessment criteria.
method: Prompt an LLM with scar-scoring criteria to generate deterministic Python feature-extraction code.
Extract low-dimensional features from images that map to clinical concepts such as the Vancouver Scar Scale.
Train a downstream classifier on these engineered features rather than on raw images.
evidence_signal: In experiments on scar classification, the abstract reports that ScaFE consistently outperformed end-to-end deep learning baselines and black-box LLM classification under limited-data conditions.
watch_item: Performance and reliability may depend on how well the generated code matches clinical criteria and whether it generalizes across imaging settings and scar populations.
paper_title: When LLMs Analyze Scars: From Images to Clinically-Meaningful Features
